# Aikya Forge CI and publication policy

Feature/fix branches target `develop`. Promotion to `main` and publication are
separate stages: a main push starts the gated automatic release workflow. PRs and
develop pushes do not publish releases.

## Active checks

| Workflow | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| tests.yml | Python 3.10–3.13, browser acceptance and cross-platform parser contracts. |
| installers.yml | Package/installer checks on Linux, macOS and Windows, including short-entry acceptance. |
| pi-runtime.yml | Pi type checking, terminal contracts and cross-platform tests. |
| forge-native.yml | Build and accept seven native platform targets. |
| release-check.yml | Version and changelog checks for main. |
| check-asset-sync.yml | Bundled agents, skills and command consistency. |

## Native release

`forge-release.yml` runs on main pushes and manual dispatch. New versions use
VERSION and matching changelog notes from the reviewed commit; no automatic bump
is made. Publishing requires all native checks and current accepted real-provider
evidence. Manual publish=false prepares without publication; publish=true requires
main. A published version is never replaced. Retries can restore latest stable
Pages from the original tag commit without rebuilding assets. See the
[release and Pages guide](../aikya/docs/deployment/automatic-releases.md).

The inherited `release.yml`, `bump-versions.yml` and `install-pages.yml` jobs are
explicitly disabled. Changing the product name must not activate them.

Root `install.sh` / `install.ps1` select the latest stable published release and
verify its native entry against `SHA256SUMS`. Pages contains the exact verified
version-bound entry from a published release. No stable release or public installer
is created by committing these files; npm publication is not part of this workflow.

Tags use `vX.Y.Z` and reference the validated commit. Never move an existing tag.
Protect main with reviewed PRs and required checks. Retain original third-party
licenses and provenance when redistributing bundled resources.
